llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its local Ollama compression purpose, but it includes an unsafe compressed-file loader and automatic local process launching that merit review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The environment and launch scripts run local subprocesses, including shell=True checks and Ollama commands; this is purpose-aligned but broader and less hardened than necessary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation asks users to install numpy and scipy without pinned versions or hashes and points users to install Ollama separately; no malicious or typosquatted dependency name was identified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are user-visible and task-focused, with no prompt hijacking, memory poisoning, exfiltration, or hidden agent-control behavior found; the documentation is entirely Chinese, which may limit user understanding.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: launch_compressed.py can start an Ollama service as a background process, and lowrank_compress.py loads archives with allow_pickle=True, which can execute code if a malicious compressed file is loaded.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a local KV-cache compression and Ollama helper toolkit, and the scripts largely implement environment checks, compression demos, quantization, and Ollama launch helpers.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the Python scripts before installing, use an isolated virtual environment with pinned dependencies, and do not load compressed .npz/.npy files from untrusted sources unless allow_pickle is removed. Expect the launch helper to run local Ollama commands and potentially leave an Ollama service running.
llm.findings:
[TT5] expected: Passing interactive chat text to ollama run is part of the chat feature and uses a structured argument list rather than shell interpolation, so this was downgraded from command-injection concern.
[TM1] expected: Local command execution is expected for environment detection and Ollama launching, but the shell=True usage is avoidable and contributes to the Review verdict.
[EA5] expected: The llama3 model value is a documented local Ollama example/default, not an undisclosed external provider switch.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation and runtime text are user-visible usability and locale concerns, not hidden or malicious behavior.
[AST4] expected: Most subprocess calls invoke expected local tools for this purpose; list-based Ollama invocations are proportionate, while shell-based checks remain a hardening concern.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The compressed-data loader does not need pickle support for the numeric arrays it saves, so loading with allow_pickle=True is an unnecessary unsafe deserialization risk.
[AST10] unexpected: numpy.load(..., allow_pickle=True) on a caller-supplied path is a real code-execution hazard if users load untrusted or replaced archives.
[SQP-2] expected: Compressed-mode behavior is described, but the documentation should more clearly state that runtime parameters and local service behavior may change.
[T09] unexpected: The static unsafe-deserialization finding is supported by artifact code and is the strongest concrete security concern.
[T08] expected: The unpinned numpy and scipy install command is a supply-chain hardening gap, but the package names are legitimate and this is not evidence of malicious dependency use.
